subject.title: Production scaling: relaxing the single-writer session lock for multi-user deployments

question: Which supported production concurrency boundary should OpenClaw adopt after confirming the reported completion-and-delivery failure: preserve one ordered session lane with improved recovery, or introduce explicit session affinity/sharding for multi-user channel traffic?
rationale: The issue offers several materially different designs with different state-isolation, configuration, and compatibility consequences; source and current-release evidence do not establish one as a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Diagnose before redesign
options.body: Collect current-release lifecycle evidence and land a narrow fix if terminal completion or delivery release is broken, then decide whether additional concurrency is still needed.

options.title: Sponsor session affinity
options.body: Define a supported sender or channel session-affinity contract and its migration, ordering, and configuration behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep current serialization
options.body: Treat the existing single-session ordering model as intentional and improve diagnostics and recovery only.

recommendation.title: Diagnose before redesign
recommendation.body: Collect current-release lifecycle evidence and land a narrow fix if terminal completion or delivery release is broken, then decide whether additional concurrency is still needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged history connects this contributor to the closest current session-lock lifecycle repair, while final product direction remains a maintainer decision.
